definitions.mean_gap: Exact mean predicted score of fixed unseen Japanese-style references minus fixed unseen Western/Korean references. Model score units, not preference probability. Full6/6 or20/28 catalogue style populations are used for exposure counts, not these heldout mean gaps.
definitions.pairwin: Fraction of cross-style reference pairs with Japanese mean higher, ties half. Equal-weight diagnostic of style ordering, not a desired recommendation mix or human accuracy.
definitions.counterfactual: Same seed and current responses; opposite prior labels on identical earlier restaurant IDs. N0 removes history. N increases by an older-history suffix extension, preserving latest inputs.
definitions.entry_rate: Style hits in actual topK / available catalogue stores of that style. Aggregates sum hits and denominators over6 repeated hypothetical states. It is finite-catalogue exposure, not probability of user preference.
definitions.relative_exposure: (Japanese hits / Japanese population) / (other-style hits / other-style population). Value1 means equal per-store entry, not a target quota. Zero denominators are explicit undefined values, never smoothed.
definitions.known_unseen: Unseen means no restaurant ID or normalized brand has appeared in past/current responses. Known includes an observed store OR brand sibling; not the same as known/unknown style labels.
definitions.topK: regularized: actual all-catalogue conservative topK. floor: actual current-floor-eligible conservative topK. Each list uses stored order; its rank field may still be global. Card4/first1 use the actual diversity selector output.
definitions.unknown: Confirmed-food both_or_mixed and not_established stay separate. Other food statuses, including missing evidence, are not automatically wrong recommendations.
definitions.score_direction: Positive Japanese-vs-N0 and positive other-vs-N0-toward-other both mean movement in the requested past-style direction. A positive Japanese-minus-other counterfactual is evidence of sensitivity, without requiring either side to cross zero.
definitions.rank_advantage: Other reference global mean rank minus Japanese reference global mean rank. Positive means Japanese ranks closer to the top. This is global rank, not rank restricted to current food.

soft_history.definition: Same ordered40 earlier restaurant IDs and same current20 as strong N40. Strong:20/20 favored-style likes and0/20 opposing-style likes. Soft:15/20 favored-style likes and5/20 opposing-style likes. Both total20likes20dislikes. This changes synthetic response consistency, not a model history-weight quota.
soft_history.validation: All12 matched pairs checked for identical history IDs/current events/reference groups and exact15/20 vs5/20 label counts.

limits: These are hypothetical responses on a fixed real catalogue, not independent users or human accuracy. Seeds reuse restaurants; no confidence interval or significance claim is made.

Reference sets were fixed from source-menu review before the model outcomes. The heldout mean gap uses4vs4 cutlet references and17–18vs25–26 noodle references per seed; all-catalogue exposure uses6vs6 and20vs28.
A first-card or4-card equality can hide continuous score and rank-distribution changes. Conversely, a score change does not establish subjective satisfaction.
The current-only floor leaves the full mean vector and ranking scores unchanged. Its per-current-trace threshold is identical across opposing history labels; it only changes candidate eligibility.
Only stored top20 lists are available. Complete within-current-food topK or all-catalogue mean-score gaps are not reconstructed or invented.
The floor policy was developed after inspecting these scenarios. Its inclusion is a posthoc paired policy comparison, not a fresh holdout validation.
